 ...RESPONDENTS

(BY SMT. K.P.YASHODA, HCGP FOR R-1;
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:20652  CRL.P No. 2650 of 2023  SMT. SLOKA B., ADVOCATE FOR R-2)
 THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 OF CR.P.C., PRAYING TO QUASH THE FIR IN REGISTRERED IN CR.NO.69/2019 ON THE FILE OF THE 6th ADDITIONAL CHIEF METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE COURT BENGALURU FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S.498-A OF IPC AND SEC.3 AND 4 AND 6 OF DP ACT.
 THIS CRIMINAL PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

Petitioner is before this Court calling in question the FIR registered in Crime No.69 of 2019 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961.
2.
During the pendency of the petition, the parties to the lis have settled the dispute amicably amongst themselves and have filed a joint affidavit before this Court.

The parties have also filed memorandum of settlement before the family Court in M.C.No.3178/2020 and a copy of memorandum of settlement filed under Section 89 of the CPC read with Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005 is filed before this Court.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the conditions stipulated in the settlement are NC: 2023:KHC:20652 fulfilled.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 would acknowledge the same.

The joint affidavit insofar as the present petition is concerned reads as follows:
"JOINT AFFIDAVIT .... .... ....
4. We submit

that the 1st Respondent Police registered an FIR against the 1st of us in Crime No.0069/2019 for the offences punishable under section 498A, 34 of the Indian Penal Code and offences punishable under section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and the same is pending adjudication on the file of the IV Additional CMM Court, at Bangalore.

entities.text: IV Additional CMM Court, at Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
5. We submit that at the intervention of advisors, relatives and well-wishers, we have agreed to settle our disputes amicably and in furtherance to the same, we have Mr Ashish Kumar Sinha vs State Of Karnataka on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26711818/
2 entered into a Compromise and have also filed Compromise Petition in M.C.No.3178/2020, wherein the 1st of us has agreed to pay a sum of rs.28,00,00/-(Rupees Twenty Eight Lakhs only) towards maintenance/permanent alimony as full and final settlement for any claim of the 2nd of us and the 2nd of us has agreed and undertaken to withdraw all the cases (including criminal cases) filed against the 1st of us."

entities.text: Ashish Kumar Sinha vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(sic) 
3. Since the offences alleged against the petitioner is punishable under Section 498A of the IPC and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act, which are not against the State or Society, and in the light of the compromise arrived at NC: 2023:KHC:20652 between the parties as aforesaid, I deem it appropriate to obliterate the proceedings pending against the petitioner.
4. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) Criminal Petition is disposed.
(ii) Impugned proceedings in Crime No.69 of 2019 pending before the VI Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru stands quashed qua the petitioner.
